options.text: <math><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msubsup></math> ion is tetrahedral like the <math><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msubsup></math> ion and is obtained when <math><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> is bonded to proton

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is one of the most stable salts containing the phosphonium ion. It is also more stable than ammonium salts

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is decomposed by water to form <math><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> converts silver salts in solution to silver phosphide, which subsequently reacts to give free metal

solution.text:
Phosphonium iodide is less thermally stable than ammonium salts, because phosphine is less basic than ammonia and decomposition occurs at 60°C .
PH4I→PH3+HI
A. PH3+HI→PH4I
C. PH4I+H2O→PH3+H3O++I-
D. 6Ag++PH3+3H2O→6Ag+H3PO3+6H+
